# REF/ALT accessibility of LCL cCREs and co-accessible pairs

Single-cCRE tests compare that element's accessibility between REF and ALT reads. Pair tests compare the fraction of spanning reads with both cCREs open between REF and ALT. A pair difference can arise from one element's accessibility difference; it does not by itself establish a difference in coordination between the elements.

All four REF/ALT tests use a two-sided Fisher exact test and BH correction. A donor contributes to a cCRE/pair test only when it has **at least 10 REF reads and 10 ALT reads** at the chosen heterozygous SNP (open plus closed reads). The same donor-level rule applies before pooling. Within-donor BH is applied separately for cCREs and pairs; pooled BH is applied across units separately for cCREs and pairs. Positive `diff = ALT fraction - REF fraction` favors ALT. `n_samples_both_alleles` counts donors passing the 10-reads-per-allele rule.

| Unit | Within donor, REF vs ALT         | Across donors, REF vs ALT |
|------|----------------------------------|---------------------------|
| cCRE | `LCL_hsca_cre_allele_by_sample`  | `LCL_hsca_cre_allele`     |
| pair | `LCL_hsca_pair_allele_by_sample` | `LCL_hsca_pair_allele`    |

## HSCA test on CRE and CRE pairs

use a 2x2 table with REF and ALT. For a single cCRE, the columns are accessible and not accessible. For a pair, the columns are
both cCREs open and not both open, either one open or neither open

- Each donor must have at least 10 reads of each allele for the unit being tested

| Test | Question and null hypothesis | Interpretation of a significant result |
|---|---|---|
| Single cCRE, within donor | Is this cCRE more accessible on REF or ALT reads in this donor? Null: the accessible fraction is equal between alleles. | Accessibility of this element is associated with the focal allele in this donor. |
| cCRE pair, within donor | Are both cCREs open together more often on REF or ALT reads in this donor? Null: the both-open fraction is equal between alleles among reads covering both elements. | Joint accessibility differs between alleles in this donor |
| Single cCRE, pooled across donors | Is this cCRE's accessible fraction different between REF and ALT after summing eligible donor counts? Null: the pooled accessible fractions are equal. | There is an aggregate allele-associated accessibility difference at this element. |
| cCRE pair, pooled across donors | Is the both-open fraction different between REF and ALT after summing eligible donor counts? Null: the pooled both-open fractions are equal. | There is an aggregate allele-associated difference in joint accessibility of this pair. |

Within-donor tests receive BH correction across tested cCREs or pairs separately in each donor. Pooled tests receive BH correction across tested cCREs or pairs separately

VCF file: `/project/spott/1_Shared_projects/LCL_Fiber_seq/preprocess_final_merged_samples/AL6_bc2162_19093/AL6_bc2162_19093.5mC.6mA.aligned.phased.vcf.gz`

| Column                        | Meaning                                                                 |
|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `#CHROM`                      | Chromosome, such as `chr1`.                                             |
| `POS`                         | **1-based** genomic position, unlike a BED start coordinate.            |
| `ID`                          | Variant identifier, such as an rsID; `.` means missing.                 |
| `REF`                         | Reference allele.                                                       |
| `ALT`                         | Alternative allele(s); multiple alternatives are comma-separated.       |
| `QUAL`                        | Variant-level Phred-scaled quality; `.` means unavailable.              |
| `FILTER`                      | Variant filtering result. `PASS` means it passed the applied filters.   |
| `INFO`                        | Semicolon-separated variant annotations, such as `AF=0.0168067`.        |
| `FORMAT`                      | Colon-separated names defining the fields in each sample’s cell.        |
| `NA19093`, other sample names | That sample’s genotype and any additional fields specified by `FORMAT`. |

| `GT`   | Interpretation                                           |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `0/0`  | Homozygous REF.                                          |
| `0/1`  | Heterozygous, unphased.                                  |
| `0\|1` | Phased: first haplotype carries REF, second carries ALT. |
| `1\|0` | Phased: first haplotype carries ALT, second carries REF. |
| `1/1`  | Homozygous first ALT.                                    |
| `./.`  | Missing genotype.                                        |

**ONLY ONE SNP PER CRE IS KEPT**, which is the het SNV shared by the most samples **SNP in CRE pair** prefer the SNP heterozygous in more samples, then closer to its own cCRE centre

## CRE and CRE pair allele specific chromatin accessibility

| R object | File | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `cre_allele_by_sample` | `LCL_hsca_cre_allele_by_sample.tsv.gz` | One row per tested cCRE per donor |
| `pair_allele_by_sample` | `LCL_hsca_pair_allele_by_sample.tsv.gz` | One row per tested cCRE pair per donor |
| `cre_allele` | `LCL_hsca_cre_allele.tsv.gz` | Pooled REF/ALT results for each cCRE with a selected SNP |
| `pair_allele` | `LCL_hsca_pair_allele.tsv.gz` | Pooled REF/ALT results for each pair with a selected SNP |

```{r sample-tallies}
tally = function(dt, name) {
  dt[, .(tested = .N, skewed = sum(status != "ns")), by = sample_name][
    , setnames(.SD, c("tested", "skewed"), paste0(name, c("_tested", "_skewed")))]
}

sample_tallies = Reduce(function(a, b) merge(a, b, by = "sample_name", all = TRUE), list(
  tally(cre_allele_by_sample, "cre_allele"),
  tally(pair_allele_by_sample, "pair_allele")))
for (j in setdiff(names(sample_tallies), "sample_name")) set(sample_tallies, which(is.na(sample_tallies[[j]])), j, 0L)
fwrite(sample_tallies, file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_sample_tallies.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(sample_tallies)

pooled_tallies = data.table(
  table = c("LCL_hsca_cre_allele", "LCL_hsca_pair_allele"),
  with_variant = c(nrow(cre_allele), nrow(pair_allele)),
  tested = c(sum(!is.na(cre_allele$p_value)), sum(!is.na(pair_allele$p_value))),
  fdr_lt_0.05 = c(sum(cre_allele$fdr < fdr_cut, na.rm = TRUE), sum(pair_allele$fdr < fdr_cut, na.rm = TRUE)))
knitr::kable(pooled_tallies)
```

### volcano and scatter plots for REF/ALT allele skew  

REF-vs-ALT accessibility and the volcano, one panel per sample. Blue dashed line: p = 0.05; red dashed line: the largest p-value with BH p \<= 0.05 in that sample

**scatter plots**

REF/ALT accessibility scatterplot
- X-axis: fraction of REF reads that are open.
- Y-axis: fraction of ALT reads that are open.
- For a single cCRE, “open” means that element is accessible.
- For a pair, “open” means both elements are accessible on the same read

| Position | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| Near `y = x` | Similar accessibility for REF and ALT |
| Above the diagonal | ALT has higher accessibility |
| Below the diagonal | REF has higher accessibility |

**volcano plots**
X-axis: ALT open fraction − REF open fraction.
Y-axis: -log2(p), higher means smaller p-value
Blue dashed line: nominal p = 0.05.
Red dashed line: the largest raw p-value passing BH-adjusted p ≤0.05 

Far from zero: a substantial accessibility difference.
High on the plot: strong statistical evidence

X-axis: ALT accessibility − REF accessibility. Right favors ALT; left favors REF; zero means equal accessibility.

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Blue dashed** | Raw p = 0.05. Observations above it are nominally significant. |
| **Red dashed** | The largest raw p-value passing BH-adjusted p ≤0.05 in that panel. Observations at or above it pass the corrected threshold. |

Outputs:

| file | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `cre_allele_by_sample_ref_vs_alt.pdf` | Single-cCRE REF versus ALT accessibility, one panel per donor |
| `cre_allele_by_sample_volcano.pdf` | Single-cCRE allele differences and significance, per donor |
| `pair_allele_by_sample_ref_vs_alt.pdf` | Pair REF versus ALT **both-open fractions**, one panel per donor |
| `pair_allele_by_sample_volcano.pdf` | Pair allele differences and significance, per donor |
| `cre_allele_ref_vs_alt.pdf` | Single-cCRE REF versus ALT accessibility pooled across donors |
| `cre_allele_volcano.pdf` | Pooled single-cCRE allele differences and significance |
| `pair_allele_ref_vs_alt.pdf` | Pair REF versus ALT both-open fractions pooled across donors |
| `pair_allele_volcano.pdf` | Pooled pair allele differences and significance |

cCRE-level analysis: For each cCRE, compare its accessibility between REF and ALT reads. Each observation in the plot represents one cCRE.
Pair-level analysis: For each pair of cCREs, compare how often both are open on the same read between REF and ALT reads. Each observation represents one pair


```{r skew-plots}

allele_labels = c("REF accessibility", "ALT accessibility", "Difference between ALT and REF accessibility")
pair_allele_labels = c("REF both-open fraction", "ALT both-open fraction", "Difference between ALT and REF both-open fraction")
panels = list(
  list("LCL_hsca_cre_allele_by_sample", cre_allele_by_sample, "ref_frac_open", "alt_frac_open", allele_labels, "p_adjust", "sample_name"),
  list("LCL_hsca_pair_allele_by_sample", pair_allele_by_sample, "ref_frac_open", "alt_frac_open", pair_allele_labels, "p_adjust", "sample_name"),
  list("LCL_hsca_cre_allele", cre_allele[!is.na(p_value)], "ref_frac_open", "alt_frac_open", allele_labels, "fdr", NULL),
  list("LCL_hsca_pair_allele", pair_allele[!is.na(p_value)], "ref_frac_open", "alt_frac_open", pair_allele_labels, "fdr", NULL))
for (panel in panels) {
  name = panel[[1]]; dt = panel[[2]]; labels = panel[[5]]; facet = panel[[7]]
  if (!nrow(dt)) next
  size = if (is.null(facet)) c(4, 3.5) else c(10, 9)
  p1 = plot_ref_vs_alt(dt, panel[[3]], panel[[4]], labels[1], labels[2], facet = facet)
  p2 = plot_allele_volcano(dt, labels[3], p_adjust = panel[[6]], facet = facet)
  save_pdf(p1, file.path(plots_dir, paste0(name, "_ref_vs_alt.pdf")), width = size[1], height = size[2])
  save_pdf(p2, file.path(plots_dir, paste0(name, "_volcano.pdf")), width = size[1], height = size[2])
  print(p1); print(p2)
}
```

#### Are pooled co-accessible pairs allele-skewed?

Pooled positives are `fdr < 0.05 & OR > 1 & co_access > expected_co_access` in the pooled table (all chromosomes) and the noXCI table; only autosomal pairs can be tested here Each test compares the skewed fraction of positives with the skewed fraction of the other tested pairs.

```{r pooled-positive-enrichment}
positives = list(
  all_chr = pooled[fdr < fdr_cut & OR > 1 & co_access > expected_co_access, CRE_pair],
  noXCI = pooled_noxci[fdr_noXCI < fdr_cut & OR_noXCI > 1 & co_access_noXCI > expected_co_access_noXCI, CRE_pair])

# A pair is allele-skewed if a within-donor or pooled REF/ALT test is significant.
pair_flags = rbind(
  pair_allele_by_sample[, .(CRE_pair, skewed = status != "ns")],
  pair_allele[!is.na(p_value), .(CRE_pair, skewed = fdr < fdr_cut)]
)[, .(allele_skewed = any(skewed)), by = CRE_pair]

enrichment = rbindlist(lapply(names(positives), function(set) {
  rbindlist(lapply("allele_skewed", function(test) {
    d = pair_flags[!is.na(get(test)), .(positive = CRE_pair %in% positives[[set]], skewed = get(test))]
    ft = fisher.test(table(factor(d$positive, c(TRUE, FALSE)), factor(d$skewed, c(TRUE, FALSE))))
    data.table(positive_set = set, test = test, n_tested = nrow(d), n_positive_tested = sum(d$positive),
               n_skewed = sum(d$skewed), n_positive_skewed = sum(d$positive & d$skewed),
               frac_skewed_positive = mean(d$skewed[d$positive]), frac_skewed_other = mean(d$skewed[!d$positive]),
               odds_ratio = unname(ft$estimate), p_value = ft$p.value)
  }))
}))
fwrite(enrichment, file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_pooled_positive_enrichment.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(enrichment, digits = 4)
```

#### Co-accessible pairs with pooled allele selectivity, ranked by p-value

These lists use the **pooled REF/ALT pair test**. Co-accessibility still requires pooled co-accessibility FDR \< 0.05, OR \> 1, and observed both-open counts above expectation. Within that set, raw allele p \< 0.05 identifies **exploratory candidates**; allele BH FDR \< 0.05 identifies the corrected discoveries. The allele BH values are retained from the original test across all tested autosomal pairs; they are **not recalculated after selecting co-accessible pairs**. Every list is sorted by raw allele p-value, with CRE_pair breaking ties. Coordinates are BED (0-based, end-exclusive). The `difference_pp` column is ALT minus REF both-open fraction, in percentage points.

```{r ranked-allele-pairs}
pair_annotation = pooled[, .(CRE_pair, chrom, cre1_start, cre1_end, cre2_start, cre2_end,
  gene_names, CRE_pair_labels, coaccess_OR = OR, coaccess_fdr = fdr,
  coaccess_p_value = pval, n_shared_reads, co_access, expected_co_access)]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(pair_annotation$CRE_pair), !anyDuplicated(pair_allele$CRE_pair))
ranked_pair_alleles = merge(copy(pair_allele[!is.na(p_value)]), pair_annotation,
  by = "CRE_pair", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
stopifnot(!anyNA(ranked_pair_alleles$chrom))
setnames(ranked_pair_alleles, c("p_value", "fdr"), c("allele_p_value", "allele_bh_fdr"))
ranked_pair_alleles[, `:=`(
  coaccessible = CRE_pair %in% positives$all_chr,
  allele_nominal = allele_p_value < fdr_cut,
  allele_bh_significant = allele_bh_fdr < fdr_cut,
  ref_n = ref_open + ref_closed,
  alt_n = alt_open + alt_closed,
  difference_percentage_points = 100 * diff)]
setorder(ranked_pair_alleles, allele_p_value, CRE_pair)
rank_pair_list = function(d) {
  d = copy(d)
  d[, rank := seq_len(.N)]
  setcolorder(d, c("rank", setdiff(names(d), "rank")))
  d[]
}
coaccessible_allele_nominal = rank_pair_list(ranked_pair_alleles[coaccessible & allele_nominal])
coaccessible_allele_bh = rank_pair_list(ranked_pair_alleles[coaccessible & allele_bh_significant])
all_pair_allele_bh = rank_pair_list(ranked_pair_alleles[allele_bh_significant == TRUE])
fwrite(coaccessible_allele_nominal,
  file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_coaccessible_pair_allele_nominal_ranked.tsv"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(coaccessible_allele_bh,
  file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_coaccessible_pair_allele_BH_ranked.tsv"), sep = "\t")
fwrite(all_pair_allele_bh,
  file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_all_pair_allele_BH_ranked.tsv"), sep = "\t")
knitr::kable(data.table(
  group = c("Co-accessible pairs with an allele test", "Raw allele p < 0.05 (exploratory)",
            "Allele BH FDR < 0.05 among co-accessible pairs", "Allele BH FDR < 0.05 among all pairs"),
  n_pairs = c(sum(ranked_pair_alleles$coaccessible), nrow(coaccessible_allele_nominal),
              nrow(coaccessible_allele_bh), nrow(all_pair_allele_bh))))


show_ranked_pairs = function(d) {
  knitr::kable(d[, .(rank, CRE_pair, gene_names,
    CRE1_interval = paste0(chrom, ":", cre1_start, "-", cre1_end),
    CRE2_interval = paste0(chrom, ":", cre2_start, "-", cre2_end), variant_id,
    REF_both_open = paste0(ref_open, "/", ref_n),
    ALT_both_open = paste0(alt_open, "/", alt_n),
    difference_pp = round(difference_percentage_points, 2),
    allele_p = formatC(allele_p_value, format = "e", digits = 3),
    allele_BH_FDR = formatC(allele_bh_fdr, format = "e", digits = 3),
    coaccess_FDR = formatC(coaccess_fdr, format = "e", digits = 3),
    coaccessible, n_samples_both_alleles)])
}
```

# significantly allele-skewed cCREs that belong to significant co-accessible pairs

Which allele-skewed cCREs participate in at least one significantly positively co-accessible pair?

CLASP1 was selected from significantly positively co-accessible pairs
with an individually allele-skewed cCRE (pooled cCRE BH FDR < 0.05, October 27 allele results)
whose focal SNV is a significant GTEx v8 LCL cis-eQTL
(`/project/spott/cshan/annotations/LCL_public_data/GTEx_Analysis_v8_eQTL/`).

This selection does not require the pair's REF/ALT test to be significant. The pair's
selected focal SNP is used for the molecule figures; here it is the same SNV as the
individual-cCRE test. The CLASP1 label is the GTEx eQTL gene, not a proven target.

| Locus | Individually skewed cCRE | Partner cCRE | Focal SNV | GTEx LCL eQTL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLASP1 | `EH38E2029449.dELS` | `EH38E3368841.dELS` | chr2:121599032 C>T | CLASP1, ALT slope -0.51, p = 2.6e-6 |

### domain, loops and CTCF annotation of selected CRE pairs


## co-accessible pairs with allele-specific chromatin accessibility

Significant positive co-accessibility: co-accessibility BH FDR <0.05, OR >1, and observed both-open counts above expectation.
Nominal allele-selective accessibility: pooled REF/ALT Fisher raw p <0.05, without requiring allele BH FDR <0.05.

# GTEx eQTL variants in co-accessible pairs

Which cCREs in significant positive co-accessible pairs contain the lead variant of a GTEx v8 LCL
(`Cells_EBV-transformed_lymphocytes`) cis-eGene? 

- Lead variant: the most significant variant GTEx reports for an eGene (`egenes` file, qval <= 0.05)

- only co-accessible pairs that survive BH correction, i.e. co-accessibility BH FDR < 0.05 (`fdr` in the 27-sample pooled table, BH across all genome-wide pairs with >= 20 fibers spanning both cCREs), OR > 1, and observed both-open counts above expectation, autosomes only

Allele-specific m6A: reads are labelled REF or ALT by the base they carry at the GTEx lead variant
(`pair_genotype_calls()`, the read-base rule of the pooled allele test). Only het samples contribute
(at least 5 informative reads, minor allele at least 2 reads and 15%)

  - `fiber_m6a_proportions()`: scores each het-sample fiber that spans the whole cCRE: its m6A calls / the cCRE positions with at least one m6A call among those fibers (not divided by A/T bases). `ref_m6a_prop` and `alt_m6a_prop` ggregate each allele's fibers: total m6A calls / (fibers x positions).

```{r coaccess-gtex-lead-eqtl}
gtex_egenes = fread(file.path("/project/spott/cshan/annotations/LCL_public_data/GTEx_Analysis_v8_eQTL",
  "Cells_EBV-transformed_lymphocytes.v8.egenes.txt.gz"),
  select = c("gene_id", "gene_name", "variant_id", "pval_nominal", "qval"))[qval <= fdr_cut]
gtex_egenes[, `:=`(chrom = sub("_.*$", "", variant_id),
  pos = as.integer(sub("^[^_]+_([0-9]+)_.*$", "\\1", variant_id)))]

# BH-significant positive co-accessible pairs (fdr = BH-adjusted), autosomes only; one row per cCRE and partner
sig_autosomal = pooled[!is.na(fdr) & fdr < fdr_cut & OR > 1 & co_access > expected_co_access &
  !chrom %in% c("chrX", "chrY")]
pair_sides = rbind(
  sig_autosomal[, .(CRE_ID = CRE1, chrom, start = cre1_start, end = cre1_end, partner = CRE2, dist, OR, fdr)],
  sig_autosomal[, .(CRE_ID = CRE2, chrom, start = cre2_start, end = cre2_end, partner = CRE1, dist, OR, fdr)])
sig_cres = unique(pair_sides[, .(CRE_ID, chrom, start, end)])
lead_in_cre = merge(sig_cres, gtex_egenes, by = "chrom", allow.cartesian = TRUE)[start < pos & pos <= end]

cre_partners = pair_sides[order(fdr), .(n_sig_pairs = .N, partners = paste(sprintf("%s (%s bp, OR %.1f, BH FDR %.2g)",
  sub("^EH38D[0-9]+\\.", "", partner), dist, OR, fdr), collapse = "; ")), by = CRE_ID]
coaccess_lead_eqtl = cre_partners[lead_in_cre[, .(CRE_ID, chrom, start, end, lead_variant = variant_id,
  egene = gene_name, gene_id, eqtl_p = pval_nominal)], on = "CRE_ID"][order(eqtl_p)]

# Aggregated m6A proportion per allele of the lead variant, het samples' full-span fibers
hsca_manifest = hsca_sample_manifest(params)
allele_m6a = function(cre_id, chrom, start, end, lead_variant) {
  snv = strsplit(sub("_b38$", "", lead_variant), "_", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  stopifnot(length(snv) == 4L, nchar(snv[3]) == 1L, nchar(snv[4]) == 1L)
  region = data.frame(region_id = cre_id, chr = chrom, start = start, end = end,
    focal_pos = as.integer(snv[2]), ref = snv[3], alt = snv[4])
  genotypes = pair_genotype_calls(region, hsca_manifest, "/project/spott/cshan/envs/Jupyter-notebook/bin/python3",
    file.path(params$code_root, "co-accessibility/LCL/hsca/hsca_functions.py"))
  het = genotypes$calls[genotype == "het", sample_name]
  out = data.table(n_het_samples = length(het), ref_m6a_prop = NA_real_, alt_m6a_prop = NA_real_,
                   n_ref_fibers = 0L, n_alt_fibers = 0L)
  if (!length(het)) return(out)
  fibers = genotypes$alleles[sample_name %in% het, .(sample_name, original_RID = read_name, allele)]
  scored = fiber_m6a_proportions(as.data.frame(hsca_manifest[sample_name %in% het]), region, fibers)$fibers[
    status == "retained"]
  agg = scored[, .(prop = sum(n_m6a_calls) / sum(n_positions), n = .N), by = allele]
  out[, `:=`(ref_m6a_prop = agg[allele == "ref", prop][1], alt_m6a_prop = agg[allele == "alt", prop][1],
             n_ref_fibers = scored[allele == "ref", .N], n_alt_fibers = scored[allele == "alt", .N])]
  out
}
lead_cres = unique(coaccess_lead_eqtl[, .(CRE_ID, chrom, start, end, lead_variant)])
lead_cres = cbind(lead_cres, rbindlist(Map(allele_m6a, lead_cres$CRE_ID, lead_cres$chrom,
  lead_cres$start, lead_cres$end, lead_cres$lead_variant)))
coaccess_lead_eqtl = lead_cres[coaccess_lead_eqtl, on = .(CRE_ID, chrom, start, end, lead_variant)][order(eqtl_p)]
setcolorder(coaccess_lead_eqtl, c("CRE_ID", "chrom", "start", "end", "lead_variant", "egene", "gene_id", "eqtl_p"))
fwrite(coaccess_lead_eqtl, file.path(tables_dir, "LCL_hsca_coaccess_cre_gtex_lead_eqtl.tsv"), sep = "\t")

knitr::kable(data.table(
  set = c("Autosomal BH-significant co-accessible pairs", "cCREs in those pairs",
          "cCREs containing an eGene lead variant", "eGenes"),
  n = c(nrow(sig_autosomal), nrow(sig_cres), uniqueN(coaccess_lead_eqtl$CRE_ID), uniqueN(coaccess_lead_eqtl$gene_id))))
knitr::kable(coaccess_lead_eqtl[, .(cCRE = sub("^EH38D[0-9]+\\.", "", CRE_ID),
  location = paste0(chrom, ":", start, "-", end), lead_variant, egene,
  eqtl_p = formatC(eqtl_p, format = "e", digits = 1), n_het_samples,
  ref_m6a_prop = round(ref_m6a_prop, 3), alt_m6a_prop = round(alt_m6a_prop, 3), n_ref_fibers, n_alt_fibers,
  n_sig_pairs, partners)])
```

Two lead-eQTL pairs are plotted with the same molecule, clustering and domain/CTCF methods
as SLFN5. In both, the pair's focal SNV used to split molecules is the GTEx lead variant.

| Locus | eQTL cCRE | Partner cCRE | Lead variant |
|---|---|---|---|
| LZIC | `EH38E1317631.PLS` | `EH38E2785168.pELS` | chr1:9943262 G>A |
| LINC00462 | `EH38E3065725.pELS` | `EH38E3065723.PLS` | chr13:48591739 G>A |
